subject: Re: MAP & cost gating — BrightPath pilot economics and timeline

Subject: Initial MAP ask — cost assumptions & gating items

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to pull together the MAP gating items they need to sign off the pilot. Two quick asks we want covered in the MAP:

1) Clear tokens-per-dollar guidance for the expected traffic profile (peak and steady).
2) Confirmation on caching and prefetch behavior (what we can cache client-side vs Redwood prefix caching).
3) Batching implications: latency tradeoffs if you enable batching at scale.
4) A simple spreadsheet we can circulate to finance for the PO.

Can you attach a short cost model and a proposed timeline for pilot kickoff + evaluation so we can align with our procurement calendar?

Sara
Sara Nguyen
Head of Product — BrightPath Health

Subject: Re: Initial MAP ask — cost assumptions & gating items

Hi Sara — appreciate the clear asks. Sharing a concise MAP attachment (MAP_BrightPath_v2.xlsx) and a CSV cost model (brightpath_cost_model.csv). High-level summary below so finance and engineering have the numbers up front.

Summary (pilot traffic assumptions)
- Avg concurrent users for pilot: 120
- Avg requests per user/day: 18
- Avg tokens per request (prompt + response): 420 tokens
- Peak QPS (burst): ~60 rps for short windows

Redwood hosted rates used in model
- Baseline model (rhod-XL): $0.00012 per input token, $0.00018 per output token
- Prefetch/cache hit reduction: assumed 22% effective token reduction for predictable prompts
- Batching
  - Small batch (size 8): latency +25ms median, throughput x6 efficiency
  - Large batch (size 32): latency +120ms median, throughput x18 efficiency (useful for non-interactive workflows)

Conservative unit economics (tokens per dollar)
- Uncached interactive (no batching): ~5,555 tokens per $1 (combined input+output-weighted)
- With 22% cache hit and moderate batching (size 8): ~9,000 tokens per $1
- Aggressive prefetch + large batch (non-interactive): ~18,000 tokens per $1

What matters for the MAP gating:
- If BrightPath requires sub-200ms tail for interactive flows, we should default to small batch sizes and a mid-tier model variant; unit econ will be closer to the first number above.
- If you can accept 300–500ms tails for some paths and use server-side prefetching, expect a ~1.6–2x improvement in tokens/$ versus uncached interactive.

Proposed timeline (high level)
- 7/26: MAP sign-off (covering cost assumptions, security checklist)
- 8/2: Pilot environment & sample data ingest complete
- 8/9–8/23: 2-week evaluation window (traffic ramp: start at 10%→100%)
- 8/30: Decision check (expand / scale / procurement PO)

Next steps: Please review the attached MAP and cost CSV. We can iterate numbers — Karthik and Mina are looped for a quick tech/QoS note. If procurement wants a one-page summary for finance, I can produce that by EOD Monday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@brightpath.health>
Date: 2026-07-20T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial MAP ask — cost assumptions & gating items

Looping in a couple of practical notes from the runtime team to make the MAP assumptions actionable. Inline comments on the spreadsheet and a short checklist below.

Inline operational assumptions (see CSV tab "ops_assumptions"):
- Cache semantics: Redwood prefix cache is best-effort; we recommend implementing a short-lived client-side key for session prompts (30s–2m TTL) to maximize effective hit rate for interactive assistant flows. This avoids cross-session leakage yet allows substantial savings.
- Batching policy: we expose per-route batch windows. For interactive endpoints we recommend a 10ms window (small batches ~6–10 tokens aggregated) which gives ~4–6x efficiency on our GPU pools while keeping median latency impact under 40ms.
- Failover path: when Dedicated capacity saturated, MAP should allow auto-fallback to the next compatible model tier (configurable). That reduces blackouts but can change tokens/$ assumptions by ~1.7x.

Traffic-shock sensitivity (quick numbers):
- +3x short burst without prefetch/cache: expected cost spike ~3x baseline token spend and tail latency risk — recommend reserve burst capacity (can be part of Dedicated or burst pool).
- +3x with 25% cache hit and batching: cost spike ~1.9x due to amortization and effective token reduction.

Checklist items to lock in the MAP:
- Confirm SLO targets per route (median + 95th) so we can pick batch windows.
- Decide on prefetching allowed for PHI-bearing prompts (requires security review).
- Confirm whether BrightPath wants fallback to cheaper model variant on overload.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk procurement/engineering through these tradeoffs.

—Karthik
Principal Infra PM — Redwood Inference

From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@brightpath.health>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, BrightPath Procurement <procurement@brightpath.health>
Date: 2026-07-22T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial MAP ask — cost assumptions & gating items

Thanks, all. The spreadsheet looks good and procurement appreciates the explicit traffic-shock numbers — that was the missing piece. A few quick confirmations before we sign:

- We'll accept small-batch defaults for interactive routes and allow up to 250ms tail at 95th percentile for non-critical flows.
- Prefetching: BrightPath product is fine with server-side prefetching for templated responses (no PHI). We'll flag PHI flows to be excluded.

Procurement asked if you can send a one-page cost summary we can attach to the PO (simple table: base tokens/$, with cache, with cache+batch). If you can send that by Monday (7/26) we'll target MAP sign-off the same day. Also, please confirm if the DocuSign link in the Drive folder can be used for the MPA.

Sara
